results.title: Nebius raises on-demand GPU prices by up to 21% | AskGPU
results.author: Saurabh Khatri
highlights:
# Nebius raises on-demand GPU prices by up to 21%

From October 1, 2026, a Nebius H100 costs $4.50 per GPU-hour on demand instead of $3.85, and a B300 $9.50 instead of $7.85. The RTX PRO 6000 stays at $1.80.

By Saurabh Khatri · Published Oct 18, 2026

Nebius raised the on-demand prices of its NVIDIA B300, B200, H200 and H100 virtual machines on October 1, 2026. Nebius’s compute pricing documentation lists the price of each GPU before and after that date. The increases run from about 17% for the H100 to 21% for the B300.

## What changed

On-demand price per GPU-hour, in US dollars, excluding VAT and other taxes:

| GPU | Before October 1 | From October 1 | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| B300 | $7.85 | $9.50 | +21% |
| B200 | $7.15 | $8.50 | +19% |
| H200 | $4.50 | $5.40 | +20% |
| H100 | $3.85 | $4.50 | +17% |
| RTX PRO 6000 | $1.80 | $1.80 | none |

Nebius bills per second, so a partial hour costs a proportional share of these rates. The documentation lists no change for the L40S.

...

Nebius’s prices page shows how much CPU and memory come with each GPU. An H100 comes with 16 vCPUs and 200 GB of RAM, an H200 with 16 vCPUs and 200 GB, a B200 with 20 vCPUs and 224 GB, and a B300 with 24 vCPUs and 346 GB. The rack-scale GB200 NVL72 and GB300 NVL72 systems still have no list price: the page says “Contact us”.

...

## Preemptible prices changed a week later

The October 1 change left the old fixed preemptible prices in place for a week. On October 8, 2026, Nebius moved preemptible GPUs to dynamic spot pricing, so those rates now move with demand. The documentation now shows only a minimum spot price for each GPU, such as “from $0.79” for an H100.

...

If you rent H100s on Nebius by the hour, your bill for the same work went up about 17% on October 1. Nebius’s prices page also says its prices can change at any time. Before you start a long job, compare the new $4.50 rate with other clouds’ on-demand H100 prices, and check whether spot capacity would suit work that can be interrupted.

results.title: Nebius did exactly what it said it would. Last week's Pulse flagged the on-demand increases Nebius had posted for October 1. Our October 4 catalog capture yesterday shows them in place, in … | Bobby Clay
results.author: Bobby Clay
highlights:
Nebius did exactly what it said it would. Last week's Pulse flagged the on-demand increases Nebius had posted for October 1. Our October 4 catalog capture yesterday shows them in place, in dollars per GPU-hour:

H100: $3.85 to $4.50
H200: $4.50 to $5.40
B200: $7.15 to $8.50
B300: $7.85 to $9.50

That changed the lowest observed H100 list price across the nine providers we track. On September 27 it was Nebius at $3.85 per GPU-hour. On October 4 it was Crusoe at $3.90.
Everything else held. Of 14,001 GPU price listings in the October 4 catalog, 13,996 matched a September 27 listing, and the 20 Nebius listings were the only verified changes above 1%.

...

These are public catalog list prices, not live quotes, and a listing does not establish capacity or orderability.

results.title: I Keep Buying More Nebius - by James Foord
results.author: James Foord
highlights:
Nebius raised prices again

On October 1, Nebius raised on-demand prices across its main Nvidia GPUs.

Specifically, the B300 went from $7.85 an hour to $9.50, a 21% increase. The older H100, H200, and B200 rose 17% to 20%.

This is actually the second increase this year. Cumulatively, the B300’s on-demand rate is up roughly 56% since May.

results.title: B300 prices are not crashing. They are splitting in two. — CheapestGPU
highlights:
The spot prints are real. On October 8, Nebius moved preemptible B300 to dynamic spot pricing with a floor of $0.99 per GPU-hour, down from a fixed $4.30 (−77%) [3].

The dedicated tier moved the other way. A week earlier, on October 1, Nebius raised its on-demand B300 rate from $7.85 to $9.50 (+21%) [3]. On GPUs.io, Verda's on-demand rate is up 27% over 30 days, Lium's 9.4%, and the market median 31.6% over 90 days [4]. Hardware has not moved either: an 8-GPU DGX B300 still anchors at $300,000 to $350,000, unchanged since Q1, and a standalone B300 at about $53,000 [5].

The useful update is the dated move on the Nebius page itself. From 1 October 2026 the on-demand H100 line goes from 3.85 to 4.50 dollars, the H200 line from 4.50 to 5.40, the B200 line from 7.15 to 8.50, and the B300 line from 7.85 to 9.50. Those four pairs are on one document, with the old rate left in place under a "before" heading. Lambda's instance rows do not carry a date. The 6.69 and 3.99 dollar figures are what that URL showed on 10 October 2026, and a revision should open the URL again rather than treat them as a contract.

results.title: Nebius Raises On-Demand GPU Prices Up to 21% From October 1: What an H100 Hour Now Costs | ServerCalc
results.author: ServerCalc Editorial
highlights:
Nebius lifted pay-as-you-go GPU rates up to 21% on October 1 — H100 to $4.50 an hour, B300 to $9.50 — the second rise since spring as AI capacity sells out.

October 12, 2026 ServerCalc Editorial 5 min read

...

## What changed

From October 1, 2026, Nebius raised its on-demand, pay-as-you-go rates across its four current Nvidia platforms. On its own published price list the per-GPU-hour numbers now read: H100 NVLink at $4.50, up from $3.85 (about 17%); H200 NVLink at $5.40, up from $4.50 (20%); B200 NVLink at $8.50, up from $7.15 (about 19%); and B300 NVLink at $9.50, up from $7.85 (21%). CPU-only servers were caught in the same round — the AMD EPYC Genoa vCPU now lists at $0.015 per CPU-hour, roughly a quarter more than before. Separately, from October 8 the provider moved preemptible capacity for these platforms onto dynamic spot pricing, so the cheap interruptible tier no longer has a fixed rate.

These are list prices for on-demand use. Committed and reserved terms are quoted separately and run well below the hourly rate; the increase lands hardest on buyers who pay by the hour with no commitment.

...

The hourly figures are small, but GPU servers run continuously and in multiples, so they add up fast. A single H100 left running around the clock for a 730-hour month now costs about $3,285 on demand, against roughly $2,810 before October 1 — close to $475 a month more for the same card. Nvidia's NVLink parts are usually taken eight to a node, and an 8×H100 box now runs $36 an hour, or about $26,280 a month flat out, up from near $22,480 — a jump of roughly $3,800 a month per node. On the newest silicon the numbers are larger again: a B300 is $9.50 an hour, so an eight-GPU B300 node is $76 an hour, more than $55,000 a month.

results.title: Nebius switches preemptible GPUs to dynamic spot pricing
results.author: Saurabh Khatri
highlights:
Since October 8, 2026, Nebius preemptible GPU prices move with demand, up to every 15 minutes. An H100 starts from $0.79 per GPU-hour, capped one cent below on demand.

By Saurabh Khatri · Published Oct 18, 2026

Nebius stopped charging fixed prices for its preemptible GPU virtual machines on October 8, 2026. Since then, the price of a preemptible B300, B200, H200, H100 or RTX PRO 6000 moves with spare capacity and demand for that GPU type in that region. Nebius announced the change in a blog post on September 22, 2026.

## How the price moves

- The spot price can change as often as every 15 minutes.
- It stays between a floor and a ceiling. The ceiling is one cent below the current on-demand rate for the same GPU.
- The console shows the current price and up to 30 days of price history before you launch.
- The same spot price applies to preemptible capacity in Kubernetes clusters and Serverless AI.

## Old fixed prices and the new range

Per GPU-hour, in US dollars, excluding tax. The spot figures are the minimums that Nebius’s documentation lists; the ceiling follows from the one-cent rule and today’s on-demand prices.

| GPU | Fixed preemptible, before Oct 8 | Spot, from Oct 8 | Spot ceiling |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| B300 | $4.30 | from $0.99 | $9.49 |
| B200 | $3.95 | from $0.99 | $8.49 |
| H200 | $2.45 | from $0.79 | $5.39 |
| H100 | $2.15 | from $0.79 | $4.49 |
| RTX PRO 6000 | $0.95 | from $0.79 | $1.79 |

The floor is far below the old fixed prices, but the ceiling is close to the on-demand rate. What you pay depends on demand at the time. The L40S is not part of spot pricing and keeps a flat preemptible rate.

results.title: Nebius Aktie: GPU-Tarife für B200 und B300 erhöht - Börse Global
results.author: Andreas Sommer
highlights:
Seit dem 1. Oktober gelten Medienberichten zufolge höhere veröffentlichte On-Demand-Tarife für ausgewählte NVIDIA-GPU-Instanzen. Die Preisliste nennt für B200 einen Betrag von 8,50 $ und für B300 von 9,50 $ je GPU-Stunde.

Die Einschränkung auf ausgewählte Instanzen ist wichtig. Es handelt sich nicht um eine belegte Preiserhöhung für das gesamte Angebot. Ebenso sind veröffentlichte Tarife von tatsächlich erzielten Erlösen zu unterscheiden. Die Preisänderung betrifft zunächst die Konditionen des Angebots, nicht einen bereits gemeldeten Umsatzanstieg.
